what_went_wrong: First v2 selection logic force-included half-rupiah visits by popping the LAST fill-pass visit to make room. One of the two dataset half-rupiah visits (2026/10/24/000423) was itself an untagged fill-pass visit at the tail, so the swap popped exactly the visit the feature was meant to protect. Result: RUN_ID=test run at 17:07Z produced a PASS report claiming half-rupiah coverage while only 1 of 2 half-rupiah visits was in the sample (the other verified nowhere against the real form).
root_cause: Membership tagging happened after the swap decision, and the pop-based swap could not protect a set it did not know belonged to the protected class. Classic order-of-operations bug: protect-then-fill was needed, not fill-then-swap.
detection: Post-run selftest asserted half-rupiah membership of the selected list and failed for 000423. No false artifact reached the orchestrator (the fixed tool ran the 17:20Z and 17:29Z validation runs and the final orchestrator run 20261011T173055Z).
fix: Rewrote selection tail: quota pass -> protected pass (all half-rupiah visits, never removable) -> fill pass. Both half-rupiah visits now in-sample; verified across two consecutive deterministic runs.
lesson: Coverage claims in gate reports must be asserted (visit X of protected class IS in the sample), not assumed from feature flags. Selection invariants deserve their own selftest before any run that will be cited as evidence.
